artifact.title: SporeApp global object lifecycle research
artifact.purpose: Static, reverse-engineering-only characterization of allocation, initialization, registration, reuse, cleanup, and teardown boundaries.
scope: Cell state, graphics, UI, and object pools
Space inventory, trading, communication, and star regeneration
OpenSpore clean-room counterparts and unresolved boundaries
exclusions: No proprietary EA source, assets, models, textures, sounds, or scripts
No replacement implementation is prescribed by this artifact
No runtime behavior is claimed without runtime evidence
No SDK name, vtable slot, or graph edge is treated as ownership proof by itself

meanings.UNKNOWN: The fact is not established by the available evidence.
meanings.APPROXIMATION: A usable clean-room value or boundary with material uncertainty.
meanings.INFERRED: A semantic interpretation follows from structure, names, or multiple indirect observations.
meanings.SUPPORTED: A static contract is supported by decompilation plus structure, field, or dossier evidence.
meanings.OBSERVED: A literal or operation is present in a targeted static body, but the semantic identity is not fully proven.
meanings.CONFIRMED: The operation or identity is established by a direct body and corroborating evidence.
meanings.VERIFIED: The fact is directly read from the binary or an explicitly pinned canonical artifact.

source_precedence: direct targeted body and exact field access
committed dossier or targeted static observation
SDK structure, function, and vtable export
canonical xref topology and call counts
triage category, cluster, or historical campaign wording
evidence_policy.runtime_rule: No lifecycle relation is VERIFIED by runtime unless a runtime evidence record is added to this artifact.
evidence_policy.ownership_rule: Ownership is asserted only when a direct allocation, intrusive AddRef/Release, destructor, pool insertion/removal, or explicit owner field establishes it. A singleton getter or vtable membership alone is insufficient.

lifecycle_stages.original: SDK structures and vtables establish types; direct constructors are known for cSpaceInventoryItem-like initialization, pool data, Cell objects, and event creation, but several global constructors remain unresolved.
Cell mode, CellGame, CellGFX, CellUI, message, and space-specific services have SDK-associated or targeted initialization paths. Initialization order is not universally runtime-observed.
Message handlers, app graphics/message services, and listener entries are registered through service maps or callback lists. Exact duplicate and removal semantics are unresolved.
Game modes use OnEnter/OnExit boundaries; Cell mode OnEnter starts the display, Update is a distinct per-frame orchestration path, and communication/trading paths are event-driven.
Pool slots are reused, Cell GFX objects are released/rebuilt, intrusive fields release-before-replace, and property/resource paths replace old references.
Cell mode OnExit resets display/global state; message and service deregistration are not fully recovered.
Cell mode Dispose, trading/inventory cleanup, pool cleanup, and service manager disposal are supported at different confidence levels. Complete global teardown order is unresolved.
